guitar.modelsText: Gibson Flying V / Vintage Fender Stratocaster
guitar.evidence: Lenny Kravitz is known for playing a range of vintage guitars including Gibson Flying V and Stratocasters; no single defining signature model.
guitar.notes: Filled from unknown with medium confidence.

tone.target: bright jangly hard-rock crunch with arena sheen
tone.profile: bright jangly hard-rock crunch with arena sheen
tone.summary: A tight signal chain using a British preamp (UK 45) for punchy crunch, followed by a clean cab simulation (UK Vintage 4x12), enhanced with light compression and delay/room reverb for arena sheen.

rig.name: Lenny Kravitz - Fly Away - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and stray noise inherent in jangly rock playing.
Provide the necessary tight riff crunch and bite without sounding overly bluesy or fuzzy.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used to emulate a slightly overdriven, punchy British tone (like an early Plexi/JTM) which fits the 'Marshall/Plexi family' clue better than pure boost.

blocks.purpose: Used as a secondary crunch layer if the Green OD isn't enough, but kept mostly off to maintain clarity and avoid heavy fuzz.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style is generally too aggressive for 'jangly,' so it is set low/off. It serves as an option for extra bite if needed.

blocks.purpose: Emulate the classic Marshall/Plexi voicing required for bright hard-rock crunch and punchy upper mids.
Provide the classic British 4x12 voicing and natural room sound for the jangly crunch.
Boost the upper mids and treble to achieve 'bright jangly' tone while cutting excessive low-end mud.
Add sustain and tighten the attack of the chords for a more 'arena sheen' feel.
blocks.gap: Compression is used here to enhance the big open chords and overall punch, which is key to the desired 'sheen'.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle stereo depth and 'arena sheen' without sounding like a wash.
Provide a subtle, natural ambience (room reverb) to achieve the 'arena sheen' without excessive wash.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the current IR for a more open, high-headroom 4x12 that better captures the 'jangly' and bright upper mids required.

proposals.recommendedAsset: open/bright 4x12 IR (e.g., Fender Twin or Celestion Greenback style)
proposals.reason: The current IR might be too dark or closed; a brighter, more open cab will enhance the 'jangly' upper mids and overall sheen.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased brightness and clarity in chords.
